_tooltips.id: Unique within your organization and used in the workflow's address. Short, lower-case and hyphenated, e.g. order-fulfillment-workflow; avoid changing it later.
_tooltips.name: The workflow's name as people see it in lists and on the task dashboard, e.g. Order fulfillment.
_tooltips.description: A note for you and your fellow designers; it does not affect how the workflow runs.
_tooltips.extends: Optional parent workflow whose roles, artifacts, tools and tasks this one inherits. A workflow cannot extend itself, directly or through others.
_tooltips.activeInstances: How many runs of this workflow are currently in progress. Set by the system.
_tooltips.version: Increases with every save. Set by the system.
_tooltips.updatedAt: When the workflow was last saved. Set by the system.
_tooltips.startEvents: The ways a run of this workflow can begin, e.g. when an order is created or every morning at 8. With none, anyone may start it by hand.
_tooltips.roles: The roles taking part in this workflow. Every role that performs one of its tasks has to be listed here.
_tooltips.artifacts: The work products this workflow handles, e.g. an order or an invoice. Every artifact its tasks read or write has to be listed here.
_tooltips.tools: The external systems this workflow may call. A task step can only use a tool listed here.
_tooltips.tasks: The tasks of this workflow, each with the role that performs it here and the tasks or events it waits for. A task can appear only once.
_tooltips.events: Events the workflow sends or waits for while it runs, e.g. waiting for a payment message or two days to pass. Tasks can wait for them like for other tasks.

_tooltips.taskDefinitionId: The task from your task catalog that takes part in this workflow. Each task can be added to a workflow only once.
_tooltips.performedBy: The one role that performs the task in this workflow. It must be one of the workflow's Roles and one of the task's Performed By Roles.
_tooltips.dependsOn: The ids of the tasks or events of this workflow that must be finished before this task can start, e.g. review-order. Empty means it can start as soon as the workflow does.
_tooltips.joinType: ALL waits for every task or event in Depends On (the default); ANY starts this task after the first of them. Ignored when Depends On is empty.
_tooltips.parallel: Tick to let this task run at the same time as other tasks waiting for the same predecessors. Unticked, such tasks run one after the other in the order listed.
_tooltips.override: Only for a workflow that extends another: tick to replace the parent's use of the same task instead of adding to it.
_tooltips.artifactStates: The state the task expects each of its inputs in and leaves each of its outputs in, in this workflow, e.g. the order is CONFIRMED afterwards. Shown in the modeler; not enforced yet.

_tooltips.roleDefinitionId: A role from your role catalog that takes part in this workflow. Removing it here only takes it out of the workflow; the role itself stays.

_tooltips.artifactDefinitionId: An artifact from your artifact catalog that this workflow's tasks read or write. Removing it here only takes it out of the workflow.
_tooltips.objectName: Optional name of the artifact in this workflow, shown in the modeler as new_order : Order. Display only; empty draws it without a name.

_tooltips.toolDefinitionId: A tool from your tool catalog that this workflow's task steps may call. Removing it here only takes it out of the workflow.

_tooltips.id: Unique within the workflow, also among its task and event ids, e.g. order-created.
_tooltips.name: Optional label shown in the modeler, e.g. Order created. Empty shows the start type.
_tooltips.startType: What starts the workflow: INPUT_ARTIFACT (the required artifacts exist), TRIGGERING_EVENT (a catalog event occurs), ROLE_DEFINITION (a person in an authorized role starts it by hand) or TIME_BASED_PRECONDITION (a moment or schedule). Only the fields of the chosen type apply.
_tooltips.eventType: TRIGGERING_EVENT only: the event from your event catalog that starts a run when it occurs, e.g. OrderCreatedEvent.
_tooltips.milestoneRef: TIME_BASED_PRECONDITION only: the milestone whose arrival starts the workflow, e.g. MILESTONE_REACHED.
_tooltips.timerType: TIME_BASED_PRECONDITION only: DATE starts once at a given moment, CYCLE starts repeatedly on a schedule.
_tooltips.timerExpression: When the timer fires, in ISO 8601: a date and time such as 2026-12-24T08:00:00Z for DATE, or a repetition such as R/P1D (every day) for CYCLE.
_tooltips.preconditionExpression: TIME_BASED_PRECONDITION only: a condition that must hold when the milestone arrives, e.g. milestone.status == 'PASSED'. Recorded, not evaluated yet.
_tooltips.authorizedRoles: ROLE_DEFINITION only: the roles whose members may start the workflow by hand. Empty means anyone may.
_tooltips.payloadMapping: TRIGGERING_EVENT and INPUT_ARTIFACT: copies data from the starting event into the new run. Key: the name to store it under, e.g. orderId; value: where to read it, e.g. $.payload.orderId.
_tooltips.requiredArtifacts: INPUT_ARTIFACT only: the artifacts, optionally in a given state, that must exist before the workflow starts. Each must be one of the workflow's Artifacts.

_tooltips.artifactDefinitionId: An artifact that must exist before the workflow starts. It has to be one of the workflow's Artifacts.
_tooltips.state: The state the artifact has to be in, as named by its state machine, e.g. DRAFT. Empty means any state will do.

_tooltips.id: Unique within the workflow, also among its task and start event ids, e.g. invoice-issued. Tasks name it in their Depends On.
_tooltips.name: Optional label shown in the modeler, e.g. Invoice issued. Empty shows the catalog event's name.
_tooltips.direction: THROW sends the event the moment it is reached; CATCH waits until the event occurs (or the timer fires) before the flow goes on.
_tooltips.eventDefinitionId: The event from your event catalog to send or wait for. Leave empty for a timer; SYSTEM events can only be waited for, never sent.
_tooltips.timerType: For a CATCH that waits for time instead of an event: DURATION waits a period, DATE until a moment, CYCLE repeats (only on a non-interrupting boundary event).
_tooltips.timerExpression: The timer in ISO 8601: PT2H (two hours) for DURATION, 2026-10-10T08:00:00Z for DATE, R3/PT1H (three times, hourly) for CYCLE — or a $.variable of the run holding it.
_tooltips.attachedTo: Optional id of a task of this workflow, e.g. issue-invoice. The event then waits only while that task is active; it must be a CATCH and takes no Depends On.
_tooltips.interrupting: Only for an event attached to a task: ticked, the event cancels that task when it fires; unticked, the task keeps running.
_tooltips.dependsOn: The ids of the tasks or events that must be finished before this event is reached, e.g. issue-invoice. Empty means it is reached when the workflow starts.
_tooltips.joinType: ALL waits for every task or event in Depends On (the default); ANY goes on after the first of them. Ignored when Depends On is empty.
_tooltips.correlationKey: MESSAGE events only, and required there: the run's variable that ties the message to this run, e.g. orderId. A THROW sends its value; a CATCH waits for a message with the same value.
_tooltips.payloadMapping: CATCH: copies data from the event into the run — key a variable name, value a path such as $.payload.amount. THROW: fills the sent event — key an attribute name, value a path such as $.orderId.

_tooltips.artifactDefinitionId: One of the task's inputs or outputs. Each artifact can be listed only once per task.
_tooltips.inputState: Only for an input: the state the task expects the artifact in, as named by its state machine, e.g. DRAFT. Empty means any.
_tooltips.outputState: Only for an output: the state the task leaves the artifact in, as named by its state machine, e.g. CONFIRMED. Empty means unchanged or unspecified.

modeler.empty: No roles have been defined yet.

_tooltips.id: Unique within your organization; workflows and tasks refer to the role by it. Short, lower-case and hyphenated, e.g. developer; avoid changing it later.
_tooltips.name: The role's name as people see it, e.g. Clerk or Developer.
_tooltips.description: What this role does and who fills it; a note for you and your fellow designers.
_tooltips.responsibleFor: The artifacts whose outcome this role owns, e.g. the invoice. Ownership only; what a task may read or write is set on the task.
_tooltips.entityRoleId: Optional matching user role of your organization. When set, only users holding that role can be given a task this role performs; empty means no check.
_tooltips.version: Increases with every save. Set by the system.
_tooltips.updatedAt: When the role was last saved. Set by the system.

_tooltips.id: Unique within your organization; tasks and workflows refer to the artifact by it. Short, lower-case and hyphenated, e.g. order-entity; avoid changing it later.
_tooltips.name: The artifact's name as people see it, e.g. Order or Fulfillment invoice.
_tooltips.artifactType: What kind of work product this is: ENTITY (a record of one of your entities), DOCUMENT (a document) or WIDGET (a screen element).
_tooltips.description: What this artifact is and what it is used for; a note for you and your fellow designers.
_tooltips.artifactTypeId: The concrete thing this artifact is, matching the Artifact Type: the entity name for ENTITY, the document name for DOCUMENT, or the widget name for WIDGET, e.g. order.
_tooltips.stateMachineId: Optional id of the state machine that governs this artifact's lifecycle, e.g. order-lifecycle. Its state names are the ones tasks and start events refer to.
_tooltips.version: Increases with every save. Set by the system.
_tooltips.updatedAt: When the artifact was last saved. Set by the system.

_tooltips.id: Unique within your organization; workflows add the task by it. Short, lower-case and hyphenated, e.g. write-spec; avoid changing it later.
_tooltips.name: The task's name as people see it on their task dashboard, e.g. Review order.
_tooltips.description: What has to be done; shown to the person working on the task.
_tooltips.performedByRoles: The roles able to perform this task; at least one. Each workflow that uses the task picks one of them.
_tooltips.preconditionRuleId: Optional id of a business rule checked before the task becomes active; while it is not met, the task keeps waiting.
_tooltips.postconditionRuleId: Optional id of a business rule that must be met before the task can be completed.
_tooltips.version: Increases with every save. Set by the system.
_tooltips.updatedAt: When the task was last saved. Set by the system.
_tooltips.inputs: The artifacts this task reads, e.g. the order. A workflow using the task has to list them among its Artifacts.
_tooltips.outputs: The artifacts this task creates or changes, e.g. the invoice. A workflow using the task has to list them among its Artifacts.
_tooltips.steps: The individual steps of the task, in order. A user step is guidance for the person; a service step calls a tool automatically.

_tooltips.id: Unique within the task, e.g. check-items.
_tooltips.name: The step's name as the person working on the task sees it, e.g. Check items.
_tooltips.description: Instructions for this step, shown to the person working on the task.
_tooltips.stepType: USER_STEP: something a person does by hand. SERVICE_STEP: the system calls the Tool and Operation below when the step is completed.
_tooltips.toolDefinitionId: SERVICE_STEP only: the tool to call. It must also be listed among the Tools of every workflow that uses this task.
_tooltips.toolOperation: SERVICE_STEP only: the id of one of the chosen tool's operations, e.g. create-issue.
_tooltips.inputMapping: SERVICE_STEP only: the values sent to the tool. Key: the tool's parameter name, e.g. summary; value: an expression over the run's data, e.g. order.title.
_tooltips.outputMapping: SERVICE_STEP only: what to keep from the tool's answer. Key: the name to store it under, e.g. issueKey; value: where to read it in the response, e.g. $.key.

_tooltips.id: Unique within your organization; workflows and task steps refer to the tool by it. Short, lower-case and hyphenated, e.g. jira; avoid changing it later.
_tooltips.name: The tool's name as people see it, e.g. Jira.
_tooltips.baseUrl: The address every operation's path is appended to, without spaces, e.g. https://example.atlassian.net.
_tooltips.description: What this tool is and what the workflows use it for; a note for you and your fellow designers.
_tooltips.type: How the system signs in to the tool: NONE, BEARER_TOKEN, BASIC (user name and password) or API_KEY.
_tooltips.secretRef: Where the credential is kept: the name of an environment variable or a Vault path, e.g. JIRA_TOKEN. Never enter the password or token itself.
_tooltips.version: Increases with every save. Set by the system.
_tooltips.createdAt: When the tool was created. Set by the system.
_tooltips.operations: The calls this tool offers, e.g. create-issue. Task steps choose one of them by its id.

_tooltips.id: Unique within the tool; task steps name the operation by it, e.g. create-issue.
_tooltips.method: The HTTP method of the call: GET reads, POST creates, PUT or PATCH changes, DELETE removes.
_tooltips.path: The address of the call relative to the tool's Base URL, e.g. /rest/api/3/issue.
_tooltips.description: What this operation does; a note for you and your fellow designers.
_tooltips.payloadTemplate: Optional JSON body of the request. ${...} placeholders are filled from the run's data, e.g. {"summary": "${order.title}"}.
_tooltips.expectedStatusCodes: The HTTP status codes that count as success, e.g. 201; any other answer fails the step. Empty means 200, 201 and 204.
